title: Orsen and the Lantern
premise: Wren Blackwood, indentured to the Meridian Trading Company since his pearl-diver father drowned in its debt, has learned to survive by being invisible. When a scarred stranger named Orsen arrives carrying letters in the handwriting of Aldous Vane—a company auditor officially dead for three years—Wren is caught between the company's hunters and Orsen's quiet crusade to expose a ledger of sanctioned drownings and stolen estates. Together with a forged-papers forger and a dockside widow who owes Wren her son's life, they must move the ledger and the letters past three checkpoints—harbor customs, the company house, and the governor's gate—before the new century's amnesty seals the company's crimes forever. Wren reaches the final gate alone, trades his own freedom for the evidence's passage, and the ledger lands; the company falls, and the found family Wren built along the way buys out his indenture with the first coins of the new era.
about_author: Xanthe Ashgrove is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging shipping ledgers from coastal trading towns, where the margins told darker stories than the columns. Their fiction is known for salt-stained prose and characters who fight institutions with patience instead of swords.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. We meet Wren hauling cargo at Meridian's docks, counting days on his indenture and keeping his head down after a foreman's beating. A glimpse of the company house's lit windows establishes the gulf between owners and owned. Emotional beat: weary endurance, and the small dignity of a hidden coin sewn into his sleeve.

chapters.title: A Stranger with Dead Ink
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Orsen collapses at the dockside tavern clutching satchels of letters in the unmistakable hand of Aldous Vane—dead three years by official record. Wren, who once copied documents for the company, recognizes the handwriting instantly. Orsen, feverish and hunted, presses the satchel into Wren's hands before company men arrive. Emotional beat: terror and reluctant responsibility.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Drowned
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, hiding in the widow Maren's loft. Reading Vane's letters, Wren learns the truth: his father's drowning boat was no accident but a debt collection, one entry among dozens. The ledger itself is hidden in the city, and Orsen, delirious, speaks only in fragments. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Forger's Basement
chapters.summary: Alternating Wren and Orsen POVs. They find Petra, a disgraced company scribe turned forger, who can replicate Vane's hand and forge passage papers. Petra tests Wren's loyalty brutally before joining. Orsen recovers enough to reveal his history with Vane—former partners, former friends. Emotional beat: wary trust becoming the first thread of found family.

chapters.title: Checkpoint One: Salt and Seals
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Harbor customs: they smuggle the copied letters out in a barrel of cured fish while the real Orsen decoys inspectors with a forged manifest. A near-discovery costs them their boat passage and forces a harder route. Emotional beat: the intoxication of getting away with it—and the first blood, when a customs officer recognizes Orsen.

chapters.title: Hunters in Company Colors
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The company's chief factor, Halloway, closes the net: dock workers interrogated, Maren's tavern watched, a bounty posted for a scarred man and a diver's boy. Wren must walk past his own wanted notice to deliver Petra's forged papers. Emotional beat: the cost of visibility—the invisible life is over, and Wren mourns it even as he chooses defiance.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Resting Place
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Guided by Vane's final letter, they recover the physical ledger from a drowned chapel crypt at low tide—Vane hid it where he hid his conscience. Orsen confesses he helped the company bury its first victims before Vane's letters turned him. Emotional beat: forgiveness asked and not freely given; Wren carries the ledger himself, his father's name inside.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Two: The Company House
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. To reach the governor, the evidence must pass through Meridian's own halls during the centennial audit. Petra forges an auditor's credential; Wren, who knows the building's rhythms, walks Orsen in as a dead man returned. Halloway nearly catches them at the stair. Emotional beat: terror sharpened into precision—the powerless moving through the house of power unseen.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Three: The Century Turns
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. New Year's Eve at the governor's gate: amnesty papers will be signed at midnight, sealing the company clean. Halloway takes Orsen hostage; Wren trades himself and the ledger's location for Orsen's release, then springs Petra's last trick—the forged credential already logged Orsen's evidence into the official record an hour before midnight. Emotional beat: sacrifice, reversal, and the bell tolling the century in.

chapters.title: The Lantern Passed On
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, weeks later. The trials gut the company; Halloway falls, and the ledger's victims' families—including Wren—receive restitution. Maren, Petra, and Orsen pool the first coins to buy out Wren's indenture. Orsen leaves a lantern on Wren's doorstep and departs to carry Vane's letters to other ports. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope—a family remains, and a new keeper of the light.
